value.rationale: A Brownian gyrator is a standard canonical two-temperature nonequilibrium model. Selectively resetting one coordinate creates a genuine choice of how circulation is observed: continuous signed area omits jump displacements, whereas time-antisymmetric position covariance includes the reset history. The theorem gives complete global sign regimes and sharp unique reversal thresholds for two measurable observables, an equal-temperature-sign paradox for all positive reset rates, and a finite-lag invariance useful for experiments with nonzero sampling intervals. These distinctions are nontrivial and structurally informative beyond routine moment computation; work and entropy production are not claimed.
